changes: Merged the former 2025 receptor sampling card into Plett Road well results because both requested the same receptor-source package.

Removed requests for records already represented by the current catalog, including DMRs, effluent PFAS reports, biosolids PFAS packages, Wexford site/topographic figures, regional groundwater literature and the available Plett Road analytical reports.

Split each active block into independently testable requirements so a supplied record removes only the requirement it satisfies and the block disappears only when all of its requirements are satisfied.

Compared the September 1 receiving-history intake against all catalog hashes, preserved one distinct audited financial report and two intake inventories, and retained every transaction-level request because none of those files contains individual delivery rows.

Expanded the receiving-history block to the seven record series identified as not yet recovered: per-load tickets, Cadillac receiving logs, Cadillac receivables, Wexford billing, the executed 2009 agreement and rate schedule, later amendments, and the dated final delivery record.

Removed the local boring, lithology and well-construction request after verifying the official EGLE Wexford County Wellogic package: 9,273 well records, 42,844 linked lithology rows and 45 wells with linked lithology within 1,000 meters of the geocoded 1121 Plett point.

Reconciled six supplied AOI address-table screenshots to pages in the complete MPART comparability report and one annotated Plett heat-map image to the official AECOM map set. These strengthen receptor/AOI context but close no requirement because the report says the study was not intended as a PFAS source investigation.

Rechecked the 24-page 1140 Plett source packet and linked it directly to the AOI event as multi-agency testing by EGLE, Merit and Cyclopure. The packet preserves repeated results and collection times but does not close a queue requirement because it lacks chain-of-custody forms and 25 pages of EGLE Work Order 2509147.

Reconciled the supplied 26-page EGLE Complete Results PDF to the exact existing A13 compilation by SHA-256. The canonical record is now hosted locally with its full download and first-page preview, and a conservative timeline event links the address and LDFA result rounds. No request closes because the address labels are anonymized and the compilation lacks the coordinate crosswalk, COCs and synchronized source-to-receptor field package.

Verified the three supplied USGS station 04121241 CSVs as exact members of the established Clam River at Plett Road ZIP export and exposed each table for direct review. No request closes because the ten discrete surface-water discharge observations contain no PFAS results, groundwater gradient, hydraulic tests, receptor field/QC package or delivery history.

The 24-page EGLE comparability source packet does not satisfy the request for the complete 49-page Work Order 2509147.
The secondary Plett well summary does not satisfy the request for an official or driller-certified completion log.
Regional USGS groundwater models and the 2012 USGS Cadillac North topographic map do not satisfy the request for a site-specific source-to-Plett groundwater-flow map.

The Wellogic package satisfies the local well-construction and lithology request but does not supply the certified 1140 Plett completion record, surveyed synoptic water levels, hydraulic tests or a site-specific groundwater-flow map.
Evidence intake manifests and not-yet-recovered inventories are tracking records; their descriptions cannot satisfy the evidence requests they enumerate.

The AOI address-table screenshots and annotated heat map do not satisfy the source-to-receptor confirmation request: they do not provide a site-specific gradient, an explicit upgradient/cross-gradient/downgradient transect, synchronized candidate-source samples, a coordinate-to-sample-ID table or the matching field/QC package.

The 26-page EGLE Complete Results compilation preserves address and LDFA analytical tables but does not identify the anonymized addresses by coordinates, supply COCs or align a synchronized Plett/source transect; it therefore strengthens context without closing a receptor or pathway requirement.

The USGS station 04121241 CSV tables document ten discrete Clam River surface-water discharge observations and station metadata; they do not satisfy requests for site-specific groundwater gradients, hydraulic testing, synchronized PFAS sampling or source-to-receptor confirmation.
